question.text: An investor's personal balance sheet shows total assets of Rs. 65 lakh and total liabilities of Rs. 13 lakh (yielding a leverage ratio of 13/65 = 20%). Using the workbook definitions of net worth (Assets - Liabilities) and solvency ratio (Net Worth / Total Assets), what is the investor's net worth and solvency ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using NISM Series X-A pp.59-60: Net Worth = Total Assets - Total Liabilities = 65 - 13 = Rs. 52 lakh. Solvency Ratio = Net Worth / Total Assets = 52/65 = 80%. Equivalently, Solvency Ratio = 1 - Leverage Ratio = 1 - 20% = 80%. The Trap: Rs. 65 lakh is total assets, not net worth. Net worth always deducts liabilities. The other options use incorrect arithmetic or wrong ratios. The audit flagged the original because the stem said "Using the same data as above", which was not self-contained when the app shuffles or randomises questions. Note: The original stem referred to data from a preceding question ("Using the same data as above"), which broke when the question was rendered in isolation by the app. The asset (Rs. 65 lakh) and liability (Rs. 13 lakh) figures from NISM Series X-A pp.59-60 have been inlined directly into the stem, so the keyed Rs. 52 lakh / 80% answer is uniquely supported regardless of question order.
